entries.title: Proverbs 15:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Aright - Expressing what he knows prudently and gracefully. Poureth out - Plentifully, continually, and vehemently, as a fountain does waters.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wholesome - Which utters sound and useful counsels. Tree of life - Is greatly useful to preserve the present life, and to promote the spiritual and eternal life, both of the speaker and hearers. Perverseness - False or corrupt speeches. A breach - Disturbs and wounds the spirits, both of the speaker and hearers.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Revenues - Though he may obtain great revenues, yet they are attended with much trouble.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Disperse - Freely communicate to others what they know.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sacrifice - All the religious services, yea, the most costly; one kind being put for all the rest. Prayer - The cheapest and meanest services.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Destruction - The place of destruction, of which men know nothing but by Divine revelation.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Foolishness - Wickedness is meat and drink to them.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Afflicted - Of the troubled in mind. Evil - Tedious and uncomfortable. Chearful - Heb. of a good heart.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Trouble - Tumultuous lusts and passions, vexatious cares, and horrors of conscience.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: An hedge - As a way hedged up with thorns, troublesome, perplexed, and full of difficulties. Plain - Is easy and pleasant to him, notwithstanding all its difficulties.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Counsel - When men do not seek, or will not receive advice from others.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The answer - By a wise, or good and seasonable answer.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The way - The way a wise man takes to obtain life, is to place his heart, and treasure, and conversation on things above.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The proud - Of the mighty oppressors. The border - The estate, the border being often used, for the land within the borders.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Pleasant - Acceptable to God.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:27
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Troubleth - Brings God's curse upon himself and family. Gifts - Bribes given to corrupt judgment. Live - Shall preserve himself and family from ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:28
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Studieth - He speaks considerately. The mouth - Not the heart; for he rashly speaks what comes into his mouth, without the direction of his heart or conscience.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:30
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A good report - A good name. Fat - Not only chears a man for the present, but gives him such stable comfort as revives his soul, and gives vigour to his body.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:31
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The ear - The man that hearkens to that reproof which leads to life, seeks and delights in the company of the wise.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:33
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The instruction - Doth instruct men in true wisdom.
